name: Threshold Pose — The 40-Floor Vigil
creator: Emerged organically after the Forty Floors and a Waiver collapse, attributed to no single source
description: Participants stood motionless at building thresholds — doorways, elevator banks, stairwell entries — for exactly forty minutes, holding printed paper signs reading only a floor number between 1 and 40, representing a victim of the Ascent Games collapse. No chanting, no marching, just presence and stillness in spaces designed for constant movement. The trend's power was in its disruption of flow: corporate lobbies, transit hubs, and Spire-adjacent buildings became briefly impossible to navigate without encountering a still body and a number.
medium: physical presence, printed paper, neural feed documentation
cultural_impact: Threshold Pose was one of the few post-Collapse protest forms to gain visible traction in Tier 3 and 4 spaces, largely because its stillness made it difficult to legally classify as an unlawful assembly; it forced corponation security to make visible choices about removal that themselves became feed content.
controversy: Axiom Network security in three separate incidents physically removed participants from corporate-owned lobbies, citing trespass; the footage of suited security personnel dragging still, silent bodies away from numbered signs became some of the most-shared content of 2219. Two removal incidents resulted in injury and subsequent civil suits.
story_hooks: A character receives an anonymous message: the floor number on their sign corresponds to a victim who was not on the official casualty list.
Someone is organizing a Threshold Pose for a collapse that hasn't happened yet — they know something.
The original viral documentation of the lobby removals has been systematically scrubbed from every feed; someone is paying for that erasure.
